decision: The sell-out -> Nordic lag is built tier by tier before any data (config/model.yaml lag_weeks: retailer reorder, distributor to OEM, OEM to ODM build, ODM kit to Nordic; 15 / 22 / 32 weeks low / mid / high) and stays the documented prior; step 5's supply graph is its flow-weighted refinement (~19 weeks)
alternatives_considered: Set the lag at the cross-correlation peak; pick it by AIC / fit in a distributed-lag regression
reason: Mechanism first (judgment checklist 1): each tier's delay is bounded by observable inventory cover and order cycles; a fitted lag on 13-18 quarters of one cycle would carry the industry cycle and sampling noise into the chain
effect: No lag in config is set from a correlation; step 6 / 7 lag models use the reasoned lags

decision: The correlation of Nordic consumer revenue YoY with Logitech radio-category revenue YoY is reported as 'Nordic consumer revenue vs the downstream / industry cycle: timing', not as a confirmation of the chain lag
alternatives_considered: Keep 'the data agree with a 2-quarter lag'; drop the check
reason: (a) the driver is Logitech SELL-IN, so its like-with-like lag is only the upstream part of the chain; (b) the target is all consumer customers while Logitech + GN are ~16% of Nordic (~27% of Consumer, step 2); (c) common-cycle controls outside the chain (WSTS billings, US electronics-store sales) give a lag that cannot be told from Logitech's (paired-difference CIs include 0); (d) one down-up cycle: every lag from ~19 to ~36 weeks is within 0.03 of the best correlation, so the data do not pin the lag
effect: step4_report.md section 2 relabelled; investment note and model report say 'industry cycle timing'; no number changed

decision: No regression of Nordic consumer YoY on Logitech sell-in AND a cycle control (WSTS / RSEAS) to separate the chain lag from the cycle
alternatives_considered: Two-factor distributed-lag regression; partial correlation at each lag
reason: 13-18 quarters of one cycle; Logitech and the cycle controls move together (collinear), so the split would be noise with a precise-looking coefficient; Pipeline B's rule: macro / industry series are context, never a regressor
evidence: steps/step5_supply_graph/outputs/graph_vs_step4_continuous_lag.csv (controls' timing); pipelines/B_macro_industry/README.md (context and sanity checks only; nothing is a model regressor)
effect: The chain lag stays reasoned (L1); the cycle's share of the timing is disclosed (P86), not estimated

topic: reasoning first: a prior per edge x brand
decision: Before any fit, the lag of the chain is stated per edge and brand from step 5's graph: edge 1 (sell-out -> brand sell-in) and edge 2 (brand sell-in -> Nordic revenue), flow-weighted over paths and cut at the brand node (stage_lags); low / high = every edge at its grade-widened low / high lag, read as a 90% range (prior sd = range / 3.29). Edge 1 also per route (Amazon direct; via Ingram / TD Synnex)
alternatives_considered: Take the end-to-end lag from a correlation; type the tier lags in by hand (lag_weeks, L1)
reason: Judgment checklist 1: the mechanism fixes each edge's lag before data; the graph already carries the evidence per edge (inventory cover bounds by Little's law, nRF54 lead time, Logitech 10-K build split) and its grades, so the prior is computed, not re-typed, and changes when an edge's evidence changes
effect: edge_lags.csv prior columns: Logitech edge 1 ~4.6 wk (Amazon direct 3, via distributors ~6), edge 2 ~14 wk; GN ~4 / ~15 wk; all lag grade C

topic: two edges; ODM and Nordic's distributors folded into edge 2
decision: The chain is modelled as two edges with the brand as the only interior node: Amazon / Ingram / TD Synnex / other retail are edge 1 (their reorder of the brand); the ODM / EMS build, Logitech's Suzhou plant and Nordic's distributors (Arrow / Avnet ...) are inside edge 2
alternatives_considered: Model the ODM and Nordic's distributors as separate nodes with their own estimated lags
reason: No public series observes the ODM's or Nordic's distributors' orders for this chain (Merry is a single cross-check, G18; Arrow / Avnet inventory is all-vendor), so separate nodes would add lags that no data can test; the graph keeps them as edges inside the prior, where their evidence already sits
evidence: steps/step5_supply_graph/src/step4_check.py (stage_lags cut at the brand node); config/supply_graph.csv E01-E10
effect: Two estimable edges, one per observable series pair: channel index (edge 1), brand sell-in vs Nordic revenue (edge 2)

decision: Edge 1 (Logitech) = speed at which the channel's weeks-on-hand deviation from target reverts: d_t = a + c t + rho d_(t-1) on step 3's channel index; mean lag T = -13 / ln(rho) weeks (continuous replenishment sampled at quarter ends; Koyck rho / (1 - rho) quarters shown); rho by Andrews (1993) median-unbiased estimation with its exact 90% interval; OLS + moving-block bootstrap and the no-trend fit shown. GN: 8 quarters of an unanchored index -> prior only
alternatives_considered: Correlate sell-in with sell-through at fractional lags; OLS rho with a bootstrap interval; no trend
reason: Stock-adjustment model (Lovell / Blinder): sell-in = sell-out + change in channel stock, so the reversion speed is the edge's lag. The trend absorbs step 3's anchor drift (D21), which otherwise reads as rho ~ 1. OLS rho on 13 quarters is biased towards zero (more so with a trend); the bootstrap does not remove the bias, the median-unbiased estimator does (P90). Sell-through is not observed separately from the disclosed gap, so a sell-in vs sell-through correlation would be partly an identity
effect: Median-unbiased rho ~0.6 (~28 wk) with a 90% interval from 0 to no reversion: the data cannot place edge 1; OLS would have read ~10 wk

topic: edge 2 estimator: attribution-constrained with a cycle control
decision: Nordic consumer YoY = alpha + s m x(t - tau) + beta WSTS(t - kappa): s = Logitech's share of Nordic consumer (step 2 Logitech + GN share x brand split), m = step 3's slice multiplier, both FIXED (sensitivity at p10 / p90 and m low / high); x = Logitech total sell-in YoY (radio categories as robustness); kappa at WSTS's own correlation peak on the same sample (RSEAS robustness); sample = destock + normal quarters (supply-constrained excluded; destock intercept and normal-only as robustness); tau on a 0.05-quarter grid, one fixed sample, 90% profile-likelihood set and a block bootstrap (kappa re-estimated per draw); unconstrained slope shown
alternatives_considered: Free slope on Logitech sell-in (b); integer lags; pool all regimes; no control; per-regime separate fits
reason: A free slope on 16 quarters of one cycle times the common cycle (P77: slope ~5x the slice); fixing the size at what attribution allows leaves the data only the timing to decide, with 3-4 free parameters. Total sell-in starts 2021Q1, so the sample holds the 2022-23 turn (radio categories start 2022Q2: n 13). Supply-constrained quarters: Nordic revenue = wafer supply (D13). WSTS is Nordic's own tier: a pure cycle control, set at its own timing so it does not borrow the slice's
effect: Every constrained fit's 90% set covers the whole 0-52 wk range: the data neither place nor contradict edge 2's prior; free slope 1.4 vs slice 0.25

decision: Per edge: posterior = precision-weighted normal on weeks (prior sd from the graph range, estimate sd = 90% interval / 3.29); when the estimate's 90% interval is unbounded (edge 1: unit root not rejected) or covers >= 75% of the searched range (edge 2: 0-4 quarters; the wider of bootstrap and profile set), the posterior IS the prior and the report says 'data did not move it'; 'moved by' = posterior - prior mid
alternatives_considered: Always precision-weight; report the estimate instead of the prior; Bayesian model over tau with a flat-surface likelihood
reason: A bootstrap argmax on a flat surface is not a normal estimate: its narrow-looking spread (e.g. at interpolation points, P86) would pull the prior by noise. The 75% threshold (config edge_lags.uninformative_share) is judgment: an interval spanning three quarters of the range cannot place a lag. Routes of edge 1 move with their cell (the data are aggregate sell-in)
effect: All four cells: posterior = prior (edge 1 GN: prior only)

topic: totals: means add along a route
decision: Total lag of a route = edge 1 (route) + edge 2 (brand): means add; range simulated with the edges drawn independently (normal, clipped at 0) and the comonotone range (low + low, high + high) shown for edges that stretch together; routes: Amazon direct, via Ingram / TD Synnex, flow-weighted, per brand
alternatives_considered: One total from the graph's Monte Carlo only; a single end-to-end regression lag
reason: Convolution of the two edges' lag distributions has mean = sum of means; independence is an assumption (one inventory cycle can stretch both edges), so both ranges are shown
effect: Amazon -> Logitech -> Nordic ~17 wk (about 1.3 quarters); via Ingram / TD Synnex ~20 wk; flow-weighted ~19 wk (step 5 graph ~19)

topic: prior basis: order-signal lag, physical dwell shown alongside
decision: Edge priors (L4) are computed on the order-signal basis (config supply_graph.lag_answer_basis = signal): step 5's physical dwell per edge + the information delay of the buyer's planning decision (step 5 G25). The physical-only prior is kept in the same rows (prior_phys_low / mid / high) and route totals carry physical_weeks. Posterior (L8) and totals (L9) rules unchanged.
alternatives_considered: (a) keep the physical prior (answers 'how long a unit sits', not 'when Nordic's revenue moves'); (b) signal only (hides how much of the lag is assumed planning cadence, grade D)
reason: The brief's question is how long a demand change takes to reach Nordic's revenue, which travels as an order signal; the physical dwell omits review periods and forecast smoothing (P86). Showing both keeps the grade-D part visible.
effect: Logitech edge 1 prior 4.6 -> 7.0 wk, edge 2 14.3 -> 19.6 wk; Amazon -> Logitech -> Nordic total 17.3 -> 24.1 wk. Data remain uninformative (posterior = prior).
